title: Foregut, midgut, hindgut

objective.text: Identify the three parts of the gut tube and the structure that closes or links each one.

body.general: Where does the gut come from? As the embryo folds, it takes in more and more of the inner germ layer, endoderm, as a tube [f1]. The tube has three parts: foregut at the head end, midgut in the middle and hindgut at the tail end [f2]. The midgut stays tied to the yolk sac by a stalk, the vitelline duct [f3]. A thin membrane seals the head end until week 4 [f5]. Another seals the tail end until week 7, when the anus opens [f6].
body.mbbs: Folding incorporates more and more endoderm, forming the gut tube [f1]. It has three parts: foregut, midgut and hindgut [f2]. The midgut stays joined to the yolk sac by the vitelline (yolk-sac) duct [f3]. This duct is wide at first, then becomes long and narrow [f4]. Cranially the foregut is closed by the oropharyngeal membrane, which ruptures in week 4 [f5]. Caudally the hindgut is closed by the cloacal membrane, which breaks down in week 7 to open the anus [f6]. Part of the allantois is taken into the body as the cloaca [f7]. By week 5, the yolk-sac duct, allantois and umbilical vessels are gathered at the umbilical region [f8].

facts.text: Folding takes in more and more endoderm, forming the gut tube.
The gut tube has three parts: foregut, midgut and hindgut.
The midgut stays joined to the yolk sac by the vitelline duct.
The vitelline duct is wide at first and later becomes long and thin.
The oropharyngeal membrane closes the head end of the foregut and ruptures in week 4.
The cloacal membrane closes the hindgut and breaks down in week 7, opening the anus.
Part of the allantois is taken into the body as the cloaca.
By week 5, the yolk-sac duct, allantois and umbilical vessels are gathered at the umbilical region.

misconceptions.wrong: The whole yolk sac becomes the gut.
misconceptions.right: Only the part taken in by folding becomes gut; the rest stays outside, linked by the vitelline duct.

checks.prompt: Put these in order from the head end to the tail end of the gut tube.
checks.why: The oropharyngeal membrane seals the foregut at the head end; the cloacal membrane seals the hindgut at the tail end.
The oropharyngeal membrane ruptures in week 4; the cloacal membrane breaks in week 7.

checks.prompt: How is the midgut linked to the rest of the yolk sac?
options: It is not; the whole yolk sac became gut
checks.why: Only part of the yolk sac is taken in; the midgut stays tied to the rest by the vitelline duct.

adult: The tube becomes the digestive tract, opening at the mouth end in week 4 and at the anus in week 7 [f5,f6].

remember.q: What are the three parts of the gut tube?
Which gut part stays linked to the yolk sac, and by what?
remember.a: The midgut, by the vitelline duct [f3].

remember.q: When do the two end membranes break down?
remember.a: Oropharyngeal in week 4; cloacal in week 7 [f5,f6].
